papers.title: Bound Entanglement with Negative Partial Transpose Exists
papers.abstract: We show that the Werner state $ρ= (23 I - 3\,\mathrm{SWAP})/1448$ on $\mathbb{C}^8 \otimes \mathbb{C}^8$ has a negative partial transpose and is bound entangled: no LOCC protocol can distill entanglement from any number of copies of $ρ$, and even with separable operations the fidelity of a two-qubit output with a Bell state never exceeds $(1+\sqrt{2})/4 \approx 0.604$. It follows that distillable entanglement is neither additive nor convex.

papers.title: Massive Triangle in Cosmological Correlator beyond Conformal Coupling
papers.abstract: A massive scalar coupled in pairs to the inflaton generates a one-loop primordial bispectrum whose mass corrections at generic momenta have lacked closed analytic expressions beyond conformal coupling. We obtain two leading mass corrections at arbitrary external momenta in terms of multiple polylogarithms of uniform weights three and four. Auxiliary-energy dressings preserve rational time integrals, revealing unexpected simplicity despite elliptic intermediate geometry. Independent full-loop evaluations, including blinded predictions, validate the closed forms. We also determine a subleading light-field singularity and recover the heavy-mass effective theory.

papers.title: The Look-Elsewhere Effect in Searches for New Physics: from Classical Methods to Machine Learning
papers.abstract: The look-elsewhere effect (LEE) arises when the location of an effect in parameter space is not specified in advance: scanning many locations inflates the significance of the largest excess, and the local $p$-value must be corrected into a global one. A well-established framework, rooted in the work of Davies and operationalised for particle physics by Gross and Vitells, provides this correction for scans over continuous parameters. Some aspects, however, remain unsettled. The definition of "elsewhere" is ambiguous and ranges from a single distribution to an entire experimental programme. Moreover, the analytical shortcuts of the classical framework do not carry over to searches based on machine learning (ML), which are affected by an implicit post-selection bias that depends on the model's resolution and expressiveness. This review covers the LEE in searches for new physics at colliders, from its statistical foundations to these modern challenges. We discuss the corrections for continuous scans and for multiple discrete tests, illustrated with simple numerical examples, and the interaction between ML and the LEE, which we connect to the broader literature on selective inference. We highlight open problems, including the computational cost of empirical calibration for complex models and the development of analytical shortcuts for ML test statistics, and offer recommendations for reporting discovery significance in both classical and ML-based searches in particle physics.

papers.title: Time-weighted energy correlators are infrared unsafe in gauge theories
papers.abstract: Energy correlators are infrared safe because each detector weights a parton by its energy, but a weight in the arrival time makes them infrared unsafe in gauge theories. For the state created by a scalar operator that makes two partons at lowest order in a weakly coupled conformal gauge theory, we show that the correlator of two time-weighted energy detectors (the light-ray operators $\int\!du\,u\,T_{uu}$) at separated directions diverges at two loops like the logarithm of the time window. The logarithm does not come from a single soft gluon, but from a soft parton pair with comparable energies, one parton in each detector; its coefficient is a closed-form function of the angle for any matter content. In $N=4$ super Yang-Mills theory, we recover this coefficient from the two-gluon Regge term of the known four-point function and derive a simple relation to the logarithm in the charge correlator. In the planar theory the leading logarithms resum to a power of the window, set by the BFKL intercept.

papers.title: A Pole-Cut Formula for Holographic Extremal Correlators
papers.abstract: We show that the holographic spectral function of a neutral massless scalar on the extremal Reissner-Nordstrom black brane in $AdS_5$ admits an elegant formula in terms of the quasi-normal modes (QNMs) and branch-cut data. In the extremal case, the spectral data comprises the zeros of the boundary source function, i.e. the QNMs, as well as its phase discontinuity across the branch cut on the negative imaginary axis of the complex frequency plane. This formula neatly factorizes into an infinite product over the QNM poles and a factor encoding the branch cut discontinuity. We derive this pole-cut formula as the zero-temperature limit of the QNM product formula for holographic thermal correlators, with the branch-cut contribution arising from the coalescence of the QNMs on the negative imaginary axis. We also clarify the role of the near-horizon $AdS_2$ region in this context. Consistency with the OPE of the boundary correlator provides extremal sum-rules involving both the QNMs as well as the phase discontinuity function. We also find that this holographic consistency forces the asymptotic form of the QNMs to be related to the asymptotics of the phase discontinuity function. We verify our formula and these OPE constraints numerically. We also demonstrate that, in the time domain, the pole and cut factors each produce complex-time singularities, whose location is determined by the optical distance between the boundary and the black-brane singularity. We expect the pole-cut factorization structure of spectral functions to hold for more general fluctuations of extremal black branes.

papers.title: Probing Ultralight Dark Matter at the Electroweak Scale
papers.abstract: Ultralight dark matter provides an explanation for astrophysical evidence for dark matter at all scales. This non-thermal dark matter requires a misalignment mechanism to reproduce the observed matter energy density of the Universe and therefore induce oscillating, time-dependent signals. We determine the sensitivity of current and future collider measurements of the width of the Z and Higgs bosons, and show that CP odd observables such as dipole moments in $Z\to τ^+τ^-$ decays provide a better sensitivity to ultralight dark matter than atomic clocks or equivalence principle tests.

papers.title: Cosmological rigidity in $3$ spacetime dimensions
papers.abstract: We establish rigidity theorems for cosmological spacetimes in $3$ spacetime dimensions. In the setting of the Bartnik Splitting Conjecture, under the additional assumptions of null geodesic completeness and the dominant energy condition, we show that the spatial topology is either spherical or the spacetime splits as a product. Our methods rely on the theory of marginally outer trapped surfaces, known rigidity results in the presence of a timelike or null line, and more recent rigidity results in the context of Penrose's singularity theorem due to the first two authors, from which the existence of a foliation by totally geodesic null hypersurfaces can be concluded. Our second main result closes the argument by establishing a splitting theorem for cosmological and null geodesically complete $3$-dimensional spacetimes which satisfy the dominant energy condition and which admit a foliation of the aforementioned type. In its proof, we make use of the local Kundt structure of the metric and construct a global parallel generator for the null foliation.

papers.title: Fewer Parameters, Longer Runtimes: The Wall-Clock Cost of Hybrid Quantum Physics-Informed Neural Networks
papers.abstract: While hybrid quantum-classical physics-informed neural networks (QCPINNs) are often described as efficient because they have fewer trainable parameters than classical PINNs, parameter count does not measure wall-clock cost. To examine this gap on a one-dimensional seawater temperature diffusion benchmark, with the quantum circuits simulated on a CPU, we time the four cumulative stages a PINN needs (the forward pass, the first- and second-order input gradients, and the PDE-loss parameter gradient) for a classical PINN, four hybrid configurations that differ in qubit count and circuit depth, and size-matched classical controls that share the hybrids' classical layers. We find that the hybrids are 14-56x slower than the classical PINN for the forward pass and 10-97x slower for the PDE-loss parameter gradient, and even against the size-matched controls, they remain 9-85x slower. Further, over the tested ranges, runtime increased approximately exponentially with qubit count, approximately linearly with circuit depth, and sub-linearly with batch size, while for the circuit-only forward pass, a second simulator backend was 10-165x slower under the same calling pattern. Although the hybrids have 38-44% fewer parameters than the classical PINN, this reduction comes from their smaller classical layers, as the quantum circuit accounts for at most 2.5% of each hybrid's parameters. Yet parameter count failed to predict runtime even among the classical networks, since the size-matched controls, despite having fewer parameters than the classical PINN, run slower than it. Our conclusion is that fewer parameters did not mean lower cost: every hybrid took at least ten times longer than the classical PINN at every stage, and the gap grew quickly with the number of qubits.

papers.title: Entanglement and HBAR entropy in a Lorentzian non-commutative black hole
papers.abstract: We investigate how Lorentzian non-commutative smearing affects entanglement and horizon brightened acceleration radiation (HBAR) outside a black hole. For a massless scalar field, tracing over the interior partner gives the exterior quantum channel, its logarithmic negativity, mutual information, and Bell entanglement fidelity. At fixed mass and Killing frequency, increasing the smearing lowers the surface gravity, increases the accessible correlations, and suppresses the leading atomic emission probability. The horizon displacement begins at order $\sqrtΘ$, while the thermal correction at infinity begins at order $Θ$. At fixed local frequency, the redshift introduces a term of order $\sqrtΘ$ at fixed areal radius. Holding the proper distance fixed, it cancels this term and recovers the common Rindler response close to the horizon. For a freely falling atom, emission and absorption obey detailed balance at the Hawking temperature in the leading horizon approximation. Random atomic injection drives the selected mode from the vacuum to a thermal state with an exact relaxation law and nonnegative entropy production. Near equilibrium, we obtain $\dot S_{\rm HBAR}\simeq\dot A_p/4$ when the radiated energy is drawn from horizon heat, where $\dot A_p$ is the positive radiative area loss. When the radiation is assigned to ADM mass loss at fixed smearing length $\ell=4\sqrt{Θ/π}$, the result is $\dot S_{\rm HBAR}\simeq\dot A_p/[4(1-\ell/r_+)]$. The mass dependence of the exterior source thus enters the entropy per unit area lost at order $\sqrtΘ$.

papers.title: Signals from the early Universe: primordial features from the full-shape analysis of BOSS galaxies and eBOSS quasars in combination with Planck
papers.abstract: We search for primordial oscillatory features using cosmic microwave background (CMB) and large-scale structure (LSS) data, combining \textit{Planck} Public Release 4 (PR4) with galaxy clustering from the Baryon Oscillation Spectroscopic Survey (BOSS) and quasars from the extended Baryon Oscillation Spectroscopic Survey (eBOSS). For the LSS data we perform a full-shape analysis of the power spectrum multipoles with the one-loop effective field theory of large-scale structure, applying infrared resummation separately to each oscillatory component. We consider four templates: linearly and logarithmically oscillating features in Fourier space, with constant, localised, or power-law-decaying amplitudes, and fit them to the CMB and LSS data separately and jointly. We find no statistically significant evidence for primordial features in either dataset, individually or in combination. The best-fitting LSS features improve the fit by $Δχ^2\simeq-6$ to $-10$, which corresponds to global significances of at most $1.6\,σ$ once the look-elsewhere effect is accounted for. In the CMB alone, the most significant feature is reduced to $\sim2.6\,σ$. Over the full frequency range, the LSS bounds on the feature amplitudes are weaker than those from \textit{Planck} by factors of $1.4$--$3$. Combining \textit{Planck} with \textit{BOSS+eBOSS} leaves the CMB constraints essentially unchanged, because the LSS data do not favour the frequencies preferred by the CMB.

papers.title: Probing Dynamical Dark Energy with Hyper Suprime-Cam Year 3 Cosmic Shear
papers.abstract: Recent measurements of baryon acoustic oscillations (BAO) and Type Ia Supernovae (SNe) have revealed a preference for a time-evolving dark energy equation of state. Because such dynamical behavior alters both the cosmic expansion history and the late-time growth of structure, weak gravitational lensing measurements can be used to test these extended models. We present an extended analysis of the real-space cosmic shear two-point correlation functions (2PCFs) from the Hyper Suprime-Cam Year 3 (HSC-Y3) survey. Using over 25 million galaxies across 416 deg$^2$, divided into four tomographic redshift bins ($0.3 < z \le 1.5$), we constrain both a constant ($w$CDM) and a time-varying ($w_0w_a$CDM) dark energy equation of state. To break the geometric degeneracies inherent in cosmic shear, we combine the HSC-Y3 data with a CMB-independent suite of background distance probes: DESI DR2 BAO, the recalibrated DES five-year SN sample (DOVEKIE), and Big Bang Nucleosynthesis (BBN) priors. In the $w$CDM paradigm, our joint analysis yields $w =-0.936^{+0.074}_{-0.067}$, consistent with a cosmological constant. Within the $w_0w_a$CDM framework, we find $w_0 =-0.832^{+0.071}_{-0.059}$ and $w_a = -1.23^{+0.66}_{-0.44}$, representing a $2.4σ$ preference for dynamical dark energy. Although the unconstrained dark energy parameters reduce the cosmic shear-only $S_8$ constraints to smaller values, our joint multi-probe analysis agrees with the baseline HSC-Y3 $Λ$CDM structure growth amplitude. We obtain $S_8 = 0.774^{+0.027}_{-0.034}$ for $w$CDM and $S_8 = 0.772^{+0.031}_{-0.030}$ for $w_0w_a$CDM. Our results demonstrate that the weak lensing amplitude is robust to extended dark energy parameterizations, and that the dynamical dark energy signal is currently driven primarily by the geometric distance ladders, a critical consistency test for next-generation Stage-IV cosmological surveys.

papers.title: Genus one mirror symmetry and surfaces with trivial first Chern class
papers.abstract: The main goal of this paper is to study the extension of genus-one BCOV type mirror symmetry for smooth projective varieties with vanishing $c_1(X)$. We show that the naive generalization of the expectation that one can encode genus one Gromov-Witten invariants in the BCOV invariant of the mirror family cannot hold in this setup. We show this by completing the study of these invariants for surfaces. Progress had been made recently by Oberdieck's proof of the Klemm-Mariño conjecture for Enriques surfaces, which can be combined with computations of equivariant analytic torsion by Yoshikawa. We also perform the analogous study for bielliptic surfaces. Both of these cases present a sign issue not present in the known trivial canonical bundle cases, which we show implies that the mirror symmetry predictions cannot hold for varieties with torsion canonical bundle, even up to sign.

papers.title: Gravitational collapse to extremal black holes with $Λ>0$: counterexamples to the third law without charge
papers.abstract: We study the dynamical formation of the extremal Schwarzschild-de Sitter solution, in both its time orientations, and the related Nariai solution. We prove that there exist spherically symmetric, regular Cauchy data for the Einstein-scalar field system with $\mathbb S^3$ topology, for any scalar field mass $\mathfrak{m}\geq 0$, that lead to the formation of an exactly extremal Schwarzschild-de Sitter black hole in finite time, and that moreover the apparent horizon of the solution is exactly isometric to that of the subextremal Schwarzschild-de Sitter solution at earlier times. We also show that if the scalar field mass satisfies $\mathfrak{m}>\sqrtΛ/2$, an analogous result holds having the extremal Schwarzschild-de Sitter white hole or the Nariai solution in place of the black hole. In the black hole case, the exactly extremal Schwarzschild-de Sitter region is bounded to the future by two event horizons and can be seen as the analogue of the exterior region in the asymptotically flat case. We moreover establish that these two black hole horizons that bound the exactly extremal Schwarzschild-de Sitter region are the only event horizons present in the spacetime, something non-trivial given the existence of multi-black hole configurations when $Λ> 0$. Consequently, the solutions arising from these data can be thought to constitute, in particular, regular counterexamples to the third law of black hole thermodynamics with $Λ>0$ arising from the collapse of physically plausible matter which is moreover uncharged. Our approach to construct the Cauchy data relies on $C^k$ characteristic gluing results for the Einstein-scalar field system in spherical symmetry, in the spirit of [KU25].

papers.title: A Genetic Algorithm Approach to Reconstructing Scalar-Tensor Lagrangians
papers.abstract: Recent DESI baryon acoustic oscillation (BAO) data, combined with cosmic microwave background (CMB) and Type Ia supernovae observations, have been interpreted as evidence for dynamical dark energy whose equation of state crosses the phantom divide $w=-1$. Such a crossing cannot be realized smoothly by a minimally coupled scalar field $\varphi$, but can arise naturally in scalar-tensor theories. We present a data-driven framework that reconstructs the scalar-tensor Lagrangian directly from observations, using a genetic algorithm to evolve the symbolic expressions for the nonminimal coupling $F(\varphi)$ and the scalar potential $U(\varphi)$. Each candidate is evaluated through a forward model that self-consistently determines the expansion history, the effective gravitational coupling, and the growth of structure. Candidates are ranked by a joint likelihood of DESI DR2 BAO, Pantheon+ supernovae calibrated with SH0ES Cepheids, compressed CMB distance priors, and redshift-space distortion measurements of $fσ_8$. We restrict to the unscreened branch of the theory and impose Solar System constraints on the post-Newtonian parameter $γ$ and on the time variation of the gravitational coupling, together with a Big Bang nucleosynthesis bound on its evolution. Across 64 independent runs, the best reconstruction improves the fit relative to $Λ$CDM by $Δχ^2=-16.6$, compared with $Δχ^2=-10.6$ for the CPL dark-energy parametrization. The preferred coupling is well described by $F(\varphi)=c_1\varphi^2+e^{\varphi}(1-c_2\varphi)$. The reconstructed theory shows phantom behavior at $z\gtrsim0.5$, but it remains close to $w=-1$ at low redshift.

papers.title: Superconformal Index Identities for Dual Gauge Theories
papers.abstract: We study superconformal index identities for three classes of dual four-dimensional gauge theories. For $\mathcal N=4$ super-Yang--Mills theory with gauge groups $SO(2n+1)$ and $USp(2n)$, we prove at every rank the equality of flavored Schur indices predicted by $S$-duality, using Rains's diagonal trace transformation. For Kutasov--Schwimmer duality with adjoint superpotential $\textrm{Tr} X^{k+1}$, we prove the index identity between $SU(k+1)$ and $SU(k-1)$ with two flavors at independent elliptic nomes $p,q$, in the ultraviolet assignment $R(Q)=0$. On the locus $p=q^k$, we reduce the identity to that of ordinary supersymmetric QCD whenever the specialized expressions are generically regular. Finally, we test the dualities conjectured by Cho and Song between quiver and single-group descriptions of four families of Argyres--Douglas theories. For the rank-one $H_1$ theory we prove equality of the two full flavored indices, and for each family at arbitrary rank we evaluate the generalized Coulomb index in both descriptions, obtaining the product formula conjectured by Buican and Jiang.

papers.title: Ultralight Dark Matter Spectrum with Gravitational Focusing and Doppler Motion
papers.abstract: Ultralight dark matter can produce signals in experiments through its couplings with the Standard Model particles. The resulting signal spectrum is determined by the phase-space distribution of dark matter, which encodes information about its production mechanism and the history of the local universe. However, the local environmental effects can modify the observed spectrum and should be included in signal modeling to avoid biased parameter estimates. In this work, we investigate how the gravitational focusing by Sun and the Doppler effect due to the detector's motion modify the signal spectrum and affect inferring the underlying dark matter parameters. We analytically estimate the signal significance and perform Bayesian analysis on simulated data to demonstrate their impact.

papers.title: Global Convergence of Second-Order Methods for Physics-Informed Neural Networks in the Overparameterized Limit
papers.abstract: Solving high-dimensional partial differential equations (PDEs) constitutes a core task in many engineering and scientific disciplines. Physics-informed neural networks and the deep Galerkin method effectively leverage machine learning models to approximate solutions of known PDEs by minimizing residuals corresponding to the PDE operator alongside external constraints. Although second-order optimizers are becoming increasingly popular for training neural networks (NNs) to solve PDEs and empirically outperform their first-order counterparts in both speed and accuracy, the convergence theory for training such models is essentially confined to first-order methods. In this paper, we close this gap and develop a convergence analysis for the regularized Newton and Gauss-Newton methods. As the number of hidden units tends to infinity, the training dynamics converge in probability, with explicit rates, to the solution of a deterministic limit equation involving a Newton neural tangent kernel operator associated with the PDE. Although the limiting kernel operator admits no spectral gap, we prove that, in the overparameterized limit, the PDE residual vanishes as training proceeds, and, under mild assumptions, the NN converges to the PDE solution. We further show that, provided a sufficiently small regularization parameter, the projection of the residual onto any fixed number of leading eigenfunctions decays exponentially fast, demonstrating that this hyperparameter acts as a spectral filter: it lifts the convergence rates of high-frequency components toward those of low-frequency ones, thereby mitigating the spectral bias inherent in gradient descent. Mathematical challenges arise from the implicit parameter update involving a linear system whose dimension increases with the NN width and, for Newton's method, a potentially indefinite Hessian, as well as from the PDE operator entering the kernel.

papers.title: Black hole entropy from angular holonomies of Sine-Gordon soliton lattices in AdS$_3$
papers.abstract: We construct boundary conditions for AdS$_3$ gravity that realize Sine-Gordon dynamics. For a periodic soliton lattice at fixed winding, we relate the angular holonomy to the exact acoustic dispersion by continuing the Bloch momentum through the zero-frequency band edge associated with rigid translation of the lattice. For suitable embedding angles, the stable vacuum has a regular BTZ geometry. When only one chiral sector carries winding, we construct a family whose asymptotic region extends to a BTZ black hole. As the spectral parameter of the winding sector tends to the corresponding band edge, the black hole approaches extremality. The leading correction to the extremal entropy is linear in the Hawking temperature defined with respect to laboratory time, with a coefficient inversely proportional to the sound velocity of the lattice. The same inverse-velocity dependence appears in the low-temperature entropy of one-dimensional quantum fluids.

papers.title: Inverted Pendulum in the Sky: Floquet Stabilization of Cosmological Axions
papers.abstract: Many cosmological scenarios require a scalar field to sit near the top of its potential, which usually requires a fine-tuned initial condition. We ask whether the hilltop of an axion potential can be dynamically stabilized by a rapidly oscillating coupling, as for the inverted pendulum of Kapitza, and to what extent this can reduce the fine-tuning. Using Floquet theory, we determine the stability window of the hilltop and analyze several realizations: an oscillating coupling, a spinning or oscillating second field, and a gyroscopic analogue, an inverted spinning top realized by a sigma model on a squashed three-sphere. In an expanding Universe the stabilized phase lasts for a number of $e$-folds logarithmic in the hierarchy of scales, independently of the cosmological background. Classifying the stabilizers by how their effective frequency redshifts, we show that in these realizations the hilltop cannot both attract the field and leave it frozen by the Hubble friction during radiation or matter domination, and that during inflation the attraction is limited by the Hubble friction and the energy budget. Thus the simple realizations studied here do not generically remove the hilltop fine-tuning. They can instead delay the onset of the oscillation and enhance the relic abundance as $n_φ/n_{φ,{\rm std}}\propto(\tilde m/H_c)^{3/2}$ in radiation domination. We discuss the implications for axion dark matter, inflation, quintessence and curvatons.

papers.title: Native higher-order optimization with entropy quantum computing
papers.abstract: Higher-order interactions are common in applied optimization: parity checks, radar-code sidelobes, portfolio skewness and kurtosis, and marketing-channel synergies all yield cubic or quartic objectives. Quantum annealers and most Ising machines accept only quadratic objectives, and gate-based quantum processors build every higher-order term from two-qubit gates. Entropy quantum computing, realized in the hybrid photonic-electronic Dirac-3S system, accepts polynomials of degree up to five with all-to-all coupling over binary, integer or simplex-constrained continuous variables. No user-supplied quadratization or circuit compilation is needed. We formulate four industrial use cases as six cubic and quartic instances, run them on Dirac-3S with 30 samples each, and score every sample against a certified optimum or a classical best-known value. We also estimate their cost on quantum annealers, superconducting grids and trapped-ion registers under standard mappings. For the two densest instances, a portfolio with about 80,000 terms and a budget allocation with 360,000 terms, the quadratized problems need embeddings far beyond current annealers, over $10^5$ physical qubits for the portfolio alone, and one phase-separation layer costs over $10^6$ two-qubit gates before optimization. Dirac-3S ran all six natively and returned feasible, distinct solutions. All samples of the binary instances are single-flip local minima. The best portfolio sample lies within 0.32% of the best-known value and the best budget sample 15% above it, but no sample reached its reference. Classical solvers reach the references within minutes at these sizes, and random starts followed by a local polish reach comparable or better values, so the advantage established here is one of expressibility and mapping cost, not of solution quality. Whether it extends to time to solution at larger sizes remains open.

papers.title: Robin--Hadamard states for unstable field in half-Minkowski spacetime
papers.abstract: We investigate the quantization of a real massless scalar field in four-dimensional half-Minkowski spacetime subject to an attractive Robin boundary condition. We show that the unstable modes, required for classical spectral completeness, are also essential to recover the canonical commutation relations (CCR) of the complete quantum field. By specifying the Cauchy covariances of the unstable sector, we construct a family of positive quasifree states compatible with the conservation of total energy. Within this family, positivity is incompatible with stationarity, so that the resulting states necessarily break the time-translation symmetry of the background. We also obtain a closed position-space representation of the two-point function for the chosen stable vacuum sector, including the contribution fixed by the CCR in the unstable sector. The resulting expression exhibits the direct and reflected singularities, including Robin-dependent logarithmic terms. Since the remaining unstable contribution is smooth, all states in the constructed family share the same singularity structure, consistent with the Robin--Hadamard framework.

papers.title: Semiclassical causal geodesics: Schwarzschild spacetime case
papers.abstract: We propose an extension of the integral quantization, applied previously to the semiclassical description of a test particle in the flat Minkowski spacetime, to the Schwarzschild spacetime. This extension yields a local integral quantization. We calculate the transition amplitudes between coherent states of a particle in a mass layer, which effectively leads to a Klein-Gordon-type dynamics. The calculated probability distributions reproduce locally the classical radial geodesic motion in the Schwarzschild spacetime. The local integral quantization presented here seems to be applicable to semiclassical quantization of geodesic motion in other curved spacetimes.

papers.title: Search-for-Gradient: Search-Based Restarts for Optimisation in Structured Flat Landscapes of Variational Quantum Algorithms
papers.abstract: Variational Quantum Algorithms (VQAs) are a promising class of hybrid quantum-classical algorithms that involve parameterised quantum circuits and classical optimisation. VQAs have found applications in simulation, optimisation, and machine learning. However, their scalability is hindered by flat landscapes-regions in the parameter space where gradients vanish exponentially small. In such regimes, gradient-based optimisation methods fail because parameter updates become ineffective in the absence of informative gradients. In this work, we propose a search-based restart framework to escape flat regions in structured flat landscapes, in which small trainable regions exist within a large flat landscape. This framework approaches the plateau escape as a search problem and locates trainable regions. The optimiser's parameters stop updating when the gradients vanish, and the method then searches over-sampled points to identify landscapes with nonzero gradients. We provide theoretical estimates of the number of jumps and the probability of escape from flat landscapes. This restarts the local optimisation process and avoids stagnation. We tested this framework on synthetic functions that mimic structured flat landscapes and a real quantum circuit cost landscape. Theoretical analysis and experimental results demonstrate that Search-for-Gradient improves optimisation performance in structured flat landscapes. The proposed framework assumes the existence of a trainable region with nonzero measure and will not work if it has zero measure. Our framework can be integrated with existing VQAs to improve trainability and robustness.

papers.title: Quantum Algorithm for Direct Estimation of Energy-Level Differences via Quantum Dynamics Simulation
papers.abstract: We present a quantum algorithm for the early fault-tolerant quantum computing (early-FTQC) era that estimates minute energy-level differences, such as energy gradients and molecular forces, at a lower sampling cost than existing phase-estimation methods. Such energy derivatives, accessed as the small energy difference induced by an infinitesimal parameter shift, are central to quantum simulation in chemistry and materials science. Although Statistical Phase Estimation (SPE) is well-suited to energy estimation in this era, applying it to an energy difference demands a sampling complexity that scales with the operator norm of the full Hamiltonian, which grows with system size. Our algorithm overcomes this by incorporating two time-evolution operators, corresponding to the Hamiltonians before and after the parameter shift, into a single quantum circuit, which is combined with a non-adaptive, statistically sampled reconstruction in the energy-difference domain. This reduces the relevant scale from the operator norm of the full Hamiltonian to that of the operator norm of the Hamiltonian derivative and the parameter shift, thereby lowering the sampling complexity. We further propose the joint estimation of energy eigenvalues and their differences, giving a holistic view of the energy landscape. Numerical simulations and resource estimations on prototypical systems, such as the Fermi-Hubbard model, demonstrate the resulting reductions in required resources without compromising precision. This positions energy-difference estimation as a practical task for early-FTQC devices, opening a route to molecular forces, response properties, and excited-state energy differences.

papers.title: Small-scale priors for large-scale cosmology: the case of $b_φ$
papers.abstract: Perturbative descriptions of galaxy clustering introduce free bias parameters that capture the complex physics of galaxy formation. Local primordial non-Gaussianity (PNG), parametrized by $f_{NL}$, induces a scale-dependent contribution to the galaxy bias that is proportional to $f_{NL} b_φ$, where $b_φ$ quantifies how galaxy formation responds to PNG. Accurately determining $b_φ$ is therefore essential for robust constraints on $f_{NL}$. Current analyses usually adopt a modified universal relation, $b_φ= 2δ_c(b_1-p)$, with $p$ calibrated to simulations. This relies on the accuracy of the simulated galaxy-formation model and ignores the uncertainty on $b_φ$, potentially biasing $f_{NL}$ constraints. We investigate whether $b_φ$ can be constrained from small-scale galaxy clustering using a flexible empirical galaxy-formation model. We fit an extended Subhalo Abundance Matching (SHAMe) model to small-scale clustering measurements and combine it with dark-matter-only separate-universe simulations to infer a posterior on $b_φ$. We validate the method using IllustrisTNG hydrodynamical separate-universe simulations. Without calibration on hydrodynamical simulations, SHAMe predicts $b_φ$ with a median error of 10%, compared with 38% for a fixed halo occupation distribution (HOD) that neglects the occupation response to $φ$, and 23% for the universality relation. The residual error is dominated by central galaxies near the selection threshold and persists when using the true stellar-mass assignment conditioned on the same subhalo properties. Small-scale clustering combined with a subhalo-based empirical model predicts most of galaxy-abundance response to local PNG. The remainder depends on galaxy-formation physics and should enter $b_φ$ priors as a theoretical uncertainty. This provides a route to data-informed priors on bias parameters.

papers.title: Black hole accretion flows as dark matter bolometers
papers.abstract: Astrophysical systems provide powerful probes of dark matter interactions, complementing direct-detection searches. We propose using accretion flows of the supermassive black hole as a bolometer for light DM. The kinetic energy of sub-MeV dark matter in the black hole gravitational potential can remain below the thermal energy of the plasma electrons. The colder dark matter population can therefore absorb energy through elastic scattering, cooling the electrons and modifying their emission spectrum. We integrate dark matter cooling into the advection-dominated accretion flow around M87$^{*}$ and solve the full set of thermodynamic equations to obtain the resulting temperature profile and radio-to-millimeter emission. By comparing the predicted spectrum with observations accompanying the Event Horizon Telescope campaign, we use, for the first time, the thermal energy balance of the hot accretion flow to constrain DM-electron scattering, obtaining stringent limits on keV-to-MeV DM for both heavy and light mediators.

papers.title: The type-D accelerating Taub-NUT spacetime: construction, geometry and physical properties
papers.abstract: We investigate the geometry and physical properties of the vacuum type-D accelerating Taub--NUT spacetime in the sector with vanishing Kerr rotation. We recover its normalized metric from the Plebański--Demiański family and a dressed finite binary, tracking the horizon Killing directions through the large-companion limit. The black-hole and acceleration horizons have distinct projective Killing generators, and their intrinsic horizon geometry yields a relation between polar Gaussian curvatures and cone angles that differs from that of the type-I accelerating Taub--NUT solution without requiring a matching of acceleration parameters. We establish separability of the type-D null Hamilton--Jacobi equation and construct an unwrapped radial conformal atlas with four simple-horizon extensions and five angular conformal diagrams. We also examine axial identifications and chronology-violating regions. The resulting geometrical and dynamical distinctions clarify how the two accelerating NUT families differ despite sharing their nonaccelerating and zero-NUT limits; the radial atlas is not claimed to be a unique maximal four-dimensional extension.

papers.title: Defect Correlators from Supergravity: Finding the Missing Contact Terms
papers.abstract: We resolve a puzzle in the computation of holographic correlators using supergravity when defects are present. Previous direct supergravity calculations of defect two-point functions were found to differ from bootstrap results by a set of contact contributions. We show that the discrepancy arises from two effects: nonlinear Kaluza-Klein field redefinitions in the bulk, which induce additional quadratic couplings when applied consistently to localized sources, and off-shell terms in mixed bulk--defect vertices, which can collapse internal defect propagators. We demonstrate how these two mechanisms resolve the puzzle in two concrete examples in 4d $\mathcal{N}=4$ SYM, where we consider two-point correlators in the presence of a $\frac{1}{2}$-BPS Wilson line and on $\mathbb{RP}^4$.

papers.title: Prethermalization of entanglement entropy in the mixed-field Ising model
papers.abstract: We study how weak integrability breaking affects the dynamics of the half-chain entanglement entropy of random product states in the mixed-field Ising model. The associated Hamiltonian depends on two parameters $g$ and $h$ determining the sizes of the longitudinal and transverse fields and has two integrable limits: the classical Ising chain $(h=0)$ and the transverse-field Ising model $(g=0)$. Weak perturbations of these limits give rise to the short-range network (SRN) and long-range network (LRN) regimes, respectively. We characterize the departure from integrable dynamics and the emergence of intermediate entanglement plateaus by melting times $T_M$ at prescribed entropy thresholds and analyze their dependence on the perturbation strength. For the SRN parameters examined away from $g=2$, we find $T_M\propto h^{-2}$ over the thresholds tested. At $g=2$, the relaxation splits into two stages: an initial departure from the integrable plateau with $T_M\propto h^{-1}$, followed by the melting of a well-defined intermediate prethermal plateau with $T_{M_2}\propto h^{-2}$. In the LRN regime, by contrast, the inverse of $T_M$ scales with exponents of $g$ close to either one or two, depending on the parameter values, the system size, and the entropy threshold, and no well-defined prethermal plateaus are observed. Our analysis distinguishes the melting of integrable dynamics from the subsequent decay of a prethermal plateau, which is observed in the SRN regime.

papers.title: Quantum Advantage in Privacy-Preserving Hypothesis Testing via Entanglement-Assisted Classical Communication
papers.abstract: Quantum mechanisms satisfying quantum local differential privacy (QLDP) have been shown to achieve a quantum advantage over classical local differential privacy (LDP) mechanisms in certain hypothesis-testing problems. While previous demonstrations have considered the transmission of quantum states from users to a server, we investigate whether this advantage can persist under entanglement-assisted classical communication (EACC), where users and the server share entanglement in advance and communicate only classical messages. We formulate an EACC-based hypothesis-testing framework and introduce measurement local differential privacy (MLDP) to protect private inputs against arbitrary shared quantum states and server-side measurements. We establish that QLDP classical-to-quantum channels admit MLDP-compliant EACC simulations and that, in the high-privacy regime, certain optimal QLDP mechanisms can be realized with one-bit classical communication, albeit using high-dimensional entanglement. We then demonstrate that a strict quantum advantage persists even when the pre-shared entanglement is restricted to a single qubit pair and each user communicates only one classical bit. Using EACC protocols based on the geometry of qubit measurements, we establish this advantage for both asymmetric and symmetric hypothesis testing and every input alphabet of size $v \geq 3$ in the high-privacy limit. The ratio of the achieved error exponent to the optimal one under the LDP constraint is at least $5/4$ for all such alphabets and approaches $3/2$ as $v$ grows. These results demonstrate that quantum advantage in locally private hypothesis testing can persist under simultaneous constraints on entanglement dimension and classical communication.

papers.title: Kiselev black hole from semiclassical gravity with conformal anomaly
papers.abstract: Investigating black hole physics in semi-classical gravitational theory is an interesting and important direction. When the backreaction of the conformal anomaly-induced effective stress-energy tensor is taken into account, the black hole spacetime can be largely altered which changes many properties of the black hole. In this work, rather than restricting our attention to the type-A anomaly, we incorporate the type-B anomaly and investigate how it modifies the spacetime structure obtained when only the type-A anomaly is considered. We find that for a specific relation between the central charges and the cosmological constant, the semiclassical Einstein equations can be solved analytically, yielding a metric that takes the exact form of the Kiselev black hole. After deriving the solution, we further discuss the properties of this new black hole solutions. Our work serves as an essential stepping stone for studying black hole geometries under the full conformal anomaly.

papers.title: Unified preparation of exact and asymptotic quantum many-body scars from Dicke states
papers.abstract: We propose a unified quantum algorithm for preparing exact and asymptotic quantum many-body scar (QMBS) states in the spin-1 {\it XY}, domain-wall-conserving, and Onsager scar models. Model-dependent isometries map the exact scar states to Dicke states and the target asymptotic QMBS states to gapless magnon excitations of the spin-1/2 ferromagnetic Heisenberg chain. Exact QMBS states are prepared by applying the inverse isometries to Dicke states. For asymptotic QMBS states, block encoding first prepares the magnon excitations from Dicke states to a prescribed fidelity, after which the inverse isometries map the prepared states back to the physical chains. At fixed target fidelity, the block-encoding success probability has a positive lower bound independent of system size and scar index, implying that a constant number of amplitude amplification rounds suffices. Our algorithm enables systematic studies of nonergodic dynamics on programmable quantum simulators.

papers.title: Revisiting the collisional energy loss of a heavy quark in an anisotropic quark-gluon plasma
papers.abstract: We revisit the collisional energy loss of a heavy quark in a quark-gluon plasma with a small momentum-space anisotropy. Within the Braaten-Thoma framework, we obtain the hard contribution in closed form and reduce the soft contribution to one-dimensional integrals. Our result demonstrates analytically that, at linear order in the anisotropy, the dependence on the artificial separation scale cancels between the two contributions. By considering the unnormalized anisotropic distribution together with two variants that hold either the parton number density or the energy density at its isotropic value, we find that the angle-dependent part of the anisotropy correction is identical in all three cases and is proportional to the quadrupole $P_2(\cosα)$, where $α$ is the angle between the heavy-quark velocity and the anisotropy direction. In addition, the sign of the anisotropy correction, which determines whether the energy loss is enhanced or suppressed relative to the isotropic result, depends jointly on the quark speed, coupling, and propagation angle. In particular, at fixed energy density, only the quadrupole term survives. For a positive coefficient of $P_2(\cosα)$, the correction enhances the energy loss for $\cos^2α>1/3$ and suppresses it for $\cos^2α<1/3$, with the opposite behavior for a negative coefficient.

papers.title: PINN-Slicer: Exploiting Rotational Symmetry to Solve the Photon Orbit Equation Around a Black Hole
papers.abstract: Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINNs) typically struggle with long-horizon domains, often requiring the network to be retrained as the domain grows. We present PINN-Slicer, a method for second-order autonomous ordinary differential equations, $\ddot{u} = G(u, \dot{u})$, which exploits the invariance of this class of equations under translations of the independent variable. A single PINN, embedded within a solution ansatz that enforces the initial conditions explicitly, is trained on a thin slice of the independent variable using Sobol-sampled initial conditions. The PINN is then deployed recursively, slice-by-slice, across the full domain. We demonstrate PINN-Slicer on the nonlinear equation that describes photon orbits around a black hole, and reach a point-by-point root-mean-square error (RMSE) below $10^{-3}$ in $u = r_s/r$ (the inverse radial coordinate in units of the Schwarzschild radius) relative to a finite-difference reference solution. A key advantage of PINN-Slicer is that a single trained network generalizes to any orbital initial condition within the training range, without retraining. In addition, PINN-Slicer can cope with solution domains that may not be known a priori.

papers.title: Empirical De-Quantization and Norm-Controlled Spectral Audit of Quantum Cognition Machine Learning in an Emerging Equity Market
papers.abstract: Quantum-inspired machine learning in econophysics describes states of financial markets through matrix Hamiltonians, using ground-state expectations to predict returns and spectral gaps to identify crises. Although early work reports encouraging advances, it remains unclear whether these stem from genuine noncommutative quantum geometry or from conventional classical regularization and scale effects. We test this in a controlled audit of matrix-form Quantum Cognition Machine Learning (QCML) and variational quantum circuits on the Moscow Exchange (2020-2025), combining daily equity data with causally lagged macro news under realistic trading costs, short-selling bans, and abrupt shifts in market regimes. By using capacity-matched operator swaps -- which progressively eliminate complex Berry phases and matrix noncommutativity down to a commuting classical Gibbs radial-basis limit under scale-invariant regularization -- as well as testing spectral indicators against radial-norm null hypotheses and untrained GUE random matrices, we isolate the contribution of each quantum element. In out-of-sample data, neither complex phases, noncommutativity, nor circuit entanglement improves the ranking of returns relative to classical controls. Once feature magnitudes are normalized, apparent crisis detection from raw spectral gaps drops below chance levels. These results show that on noisy equity panels, matrix-form QCML acts as an adaptive spectrally bounded classical smoothing kernel: it reliably integrates lagged news and curbs extreme crisis forecasts without passing economic multiple-testing thresholds, while our audit provides operator-swap and random-matrix controls for evaluating future quantum-inspired financial models.

papers.title: Decoherent Histories from Local Spectral Dephasing in Quantum Many-Body Systems
papers.abstract: We study local spectral dephasing as a mechanism for decoherent histories in isolated quantum many-body systems. We prove that vanishing projector-weighted spectral concentration is asymptotically equivalent to vanishing time-averaged local memory. With independently sampled waiting times and suitable conditions on the initial state and history weights, this local property suppresses normalized interference across complete fixed-length history families with high probability. For translation-invariant lattices, spectral estimates provide conditions under which dephasing occurs at long times. Exact diagonalization and sparse time evolution of a spin chain illustrate the results.

papers.title: TyxonQ: A Workflow Layer for Quantum Computing in Chemistry
papers.abstract: Quantum computational chemistry is often framed around a hybrid quantum solver. In practical applications, however, bottlenecks to adoption also lie in the surrounding multiscale workflow. A molecular problem may combine classical molecular mechanics and dynamics, conventional electronic-structure calculations, and a quantum solver for selected orbitals or embedded fragments. This division of work is particularly relevant when a chemically important electronic subspace is strongly correlated. The size of the electronic Hilbert space and the qubit, noise, and circuit-depth constraints of noisy intermediate-scale quantum (NISQ) devices make active-space and embedding choices central to a feasible quantum calculation. The resulting energies and gradients must remain consistent with the surrounding classical simulation. We present TyxonQ, a workflow layer that connects these levels of treatment rather than addressing only the hybrid quantum algorithm. Four integration interfaces link PySCF-compatible energy/force scanners and embedding, solver adapters, simulator and hardware backends, and classical consumers. The implementation combines QM/MM and fragment embedding with conventional CCSD/FCI fragment solvers, variational and sampling-based quantum methods, and adapters for ASE, i-PI, OpenMM, LAMMPS (through i-PI), and MDI. We describe the contracts and audit coverage, and evaluate correctness, switching cost, reproducibility, and artifact portability on small chemistry workflows, distinguishing executed paths from source-level support. The purpose of TyxonQ is to support incremental integration of quantum calculations into existing computational chemistry workflows, including those used in industry, while retaining appropriate classical treatments elsewhere.

papers.title: Cosmographic Analysis of Gravitational Baryogenesis in Running-$G$ Cosmology
papers.abstract: Gravitational baryogenesis produces a baryon asymmetry through the coupling of the baryon current to the derivative of the Ricci scalar, so its yield is set by the expansion history around decoupling. We study this mechanism in cosmology with a running Newton coupling of the asymptotic-safety type. Writing the Ricci scalar and its derivative through the Hubble rate, the deceleration parameter $q$ and the jerk $j$, we show that the yield is proportional to the kernel $K=2+q-j$, which vanishes for radiation in general relativity, and to a power of an enhancement factor measuring how strongly the running coupling accelerates the expansion at decoupling. We treat hybrid, intermediate, logamediate, emergent, bouncing and little-rip scale factors and determine where the observed asymmetry is reproduced for the $J^μ\partial_μR$ and $J^μ\partial_μR^2$ couplings; a table compares the six cases.

papers.title: Efficient Quantum Algorithm for the Generalised Geography Game
papers.abstract: The Generalized Geography Game ($GGG$) is a two-player combinatorial game played on a directed graph, where players alternately move a token along edges without revisiting previously visited vertices. In the existing literature, determining whether an arbitrary position in a graph is a winning position for either player is a well-known $PSPACE$-complete decision problem. Certain formulations of $GGG$ have been shown to fall outside the $PSPACE$-complete complexity class. While $PSPACE$-complete problems are believed to take exponential time for classical computation, quantum computation offers new possibilities. In this work, we present a bounded-error quantum polynomial-time ($BQP$) algorithm for solving the $GGG$ problem. The proposed algorithm runs in time $O(N^{2}/ε^{6})$, which is polynomial in the input size $N$, and achieves bounded error with $ε= O(1/\mathrm{poly}(N))$. This result demonstrates the potential of quantum algorithms to efficiently solve combinatorial game problems that are traditionally considered computationally hard in the classical setting.

papers.title: QPAT: A Universal Quantum Machine Learning Framework for Quantum-Assisted Training and Classical Inference
papers.abstract: Deep learning models often struggle with sharp local optima and overfitting in limited-data regimes, and exhibit limited capacity for capturing high-order, complex probability distributions. Quantum Machine Learning (QML) models, by operating in exponentially large Hilbert spaces, can efficiently represent such distributions and provide favorable inductive biases for learning, offering a promising pathway to overcome these limitations. However, their practical deployment in the Noisy Intermediate-Scale Quantum (NISQ) era is severely hindered by gradient coupling, barren plateaus, data-loading bottlenecks, and high inference latency. To bridge classical AI and QML, we propose QPAT (QCBM-Prior-Assisted Training), a universal framework that employs a Quantum Circuit Born Machine (QCBM) as a learnable generative prior to provide a task-aligned structured inductive bias during classical model training. The framework can be seamlessly integrated into any classical backbone, including LSTMs, CNNs, and Transformers. We introduce a decoupled fitness-based scoring mechanism and a stochastic "Drop-Prior" mechanism to implicitly distill quantum structural knowledge into the classical weights during training. Evaluated extensively on six benchmarks spanning time-series forecasting, computer vision, and natural language processing, our framework consistently outperforms purely classical backbones in both predictive performance and stability across random seeds; ablation studies further show that these gains are not reproduced by unstructured random priors or a classically learned generative prior. Remarkably, our approach enables completely classical inference, bypassing quantum latency while preserving quantum-enhanced accuracy, paving a highly practical path for QML deployment.

papers.title: Higgsino dark matter explanation of LZ high-recoil event from deflected AMSB with $U(1)_X$ generated $μ$ term
papers.abstract: Motivated by the recent LZ high-recoil event, we propose to study the Higgsino dark matter in a supersymmetric $U(1)_X$ framework with one charged visible singlet. The gauge symmetry forbids the bare Higgs bilinear and the cubic $S^3$ while allowing the singlet interaction that generates an effective Higgsino mass after symmetry breaking. We present the six-state neutralino mixing matrix, including the $U(1)_X$ gaugino and the singlino, and the resulting neutral Higgsino mass splitting. Different deflected-anomaly-mediated parameter regimes provide the soft-mass hierarchies needed for light, 1.1 TeV and heavy Higgsino candidates. The cosmological consequences of the messenger sector in deflected AMSB can affect greatly the thermal history of the dark matter. Late messenger decays can supplement an underabundant thermal population or dilute an overabundant one through entropy production. These possibilities are governed by a common final-yield relation: a dominating messenger must have sufficiently suppressed Higgsino production for net dilution to succeed. We organise the 500 GeV, 1.1 TeV and 100 TeV reference regimes around this condition. Direct-detection and solar-capture constraints are discussed as tests of the resulting spectrum and final abundance. The elastic bino- or singlino-like interpretation of the same event is also realized in this spectrum: the Higgsino asymmetry $|X_A|\simeq10^{-2}$ that a $248\keV$ recoil requires arises without tuning, with a spin-dependent rate lying close to the present experimental sensitivity.

papers.title: Late-time OTOCs in Toda conformal field theory
papers.abstract: We study late-time out-of-time-order correlators (OTOCs) of semi-degenerate primary fields in two-dimensional $A_{N-1}$ Toda conformal field theory. In Liouville theory ($N=2$), we find that the OTOC decays as $t^{-3/2}$ when the continuum edge dominates, correcting a previously reported constant limit. For $N=3$, a transverse contour pinch reduces the spectral integral to one dimension. Assuming that the reduced expansion is complete, in the continuous phase the regulated edge behaves as a discrete state, and the OTOC approaches a pure braiding phase. As we check numerically, the edge block is a free-field correlator in a charge-neutral Weyl frame; this explains the pure phase and is consistent with crossing symmetry. For both $N=2$ and $N=3$, a dominant discrete residue gives a constant late-time limit. For $N\geq4$, the same one-dimensional reduction violates a crossing bound on the lowest intermediate weight of a positive diagonal expansion. Hence the $N=2,3$ phase diagram does not extend to higher rank without additional contributions below the reduced continuum edge or outside a positive diagonal expansion.

papers.title: Improved Quantum Algorithms for TSP and More
papers.abstract: The traveling salesman problem (TSP) is a canonical NP-hard optimization problem. For general edge weights, the classical dynamic programs of Bellman and of Held and Karp solve TSP on $n$ cities in $O^*(2^n)$ time. To date, no $\Oh(c^n)$-time classical algorithm is known for any $c<2$. Combining Grover search with the dynamic programming technique, Ambainis et al. (SODA 2019) introduced a quantum algorithm with running time $O^*(1.7274^n)$, which is still the best known quantum time bound. In this work, we improve the running time to $O^*(1.70961^n)$. The core idea of our algorithm is to combine the framework of Ambainis et al. with the extremal set-system framework, which was recently used for classical space-time tradeoffs of TSP by Jabal Ameli, Nederlof and Wang (FOCS 2026) and Dallant and Kozma (FOCS 2026). To obtain our upper bound, we decompose the optimal tour into four consecutive subpaths of different sizes, for which, based on the idea of set-systems, the optimal values are computed using dynamic programming with small success probability and use amplitude amplification. Using the same idea, we also give a new quantum space-time tradeoff for TSP, improving the previous results of Caroppo et al. (ESA 2026) and Dallant (arXiv:2607.12374). Finally, we obtain the same quantum upper bounds for several other related problems.

papers.title: Physics-Informed Learning for Multiplayer Differential Games
papers.abstract: Computing per-player feedback strategies in $N$-player adversarial differential games is challenging as the associated coupled Hamilton-Jacobi-Bellman system is high-dimensional and generally lacks classical solutions. We address this by approximating viscosity solutions using physics-informed neural networks within a policy iteration scheme with a vanishing-viscosity annealing schedule. Theoretically, we establish an explicit $\varepsilon$-Nash guarantee by bounding per-player regret via computable residuals and prove our method reaches this stopping criterion in finite time. For two-player zero-sum games, we further establish a computable bound on the approximation error of the value function. Numerical experiments on pursuit-evasion scenarios illustrate the tightness of these computed bounds and the framework's scalability to high-dimensional environments.

papers.title: The Dirac equation in arbitrary coordinate systems and curved spacetimes - An orthonormal frames approach
papers.abstract: In this pedagogical article we discuss the Dirac equation in arbitrary coordinate systems. We explain the need for connections when dealing with spinor fields and present the practical steps needed to compute the Dirac operator in a general setting, allowing for arbitrary coordinate systems and position-dependent orthonormal gamma matrices, both of which can simplify computations in certain scenarios. The extension to include minimally coupled gravity is straightforward. Examples are provided, including constructing the Dirac equation in spherical and cylindrical symmetry (with or without gravity) and the Kerr spacetime. We also briefly comment on the advantages and disadvantages of various tetrads and orthonormal gamma matrices. This manuscript should be accessible to readers who have studied the Dirac equation at an introductory level (e.g., in Cartesian coordinates in flat spacetime with constant gamma matrices). The emphasis is on the use of orthonormal frames, since these correspond to the coordinate systems most familiar to readers when dealing with most field theories, and represent the physical frames where measurements are performed. The aim is to get the reader quickly to the point of being able to do calculations, so the presentation favors a concise, pragmatic approach over extended derivations.

papers.title: Holographic probes and Krylov complexity on asymptotically Lifshitz rotating black branes
papers.abstract: We study two types of holographic probes on a five-dimensional, asymptotically Lifshitz, rotating black hole. This geometry solves the field equations of Einstein gravity coupled to a dilaton, two axionic scalars, and a Maxwell doublet, supplemented by two vector doublets that enter the action through a parity-odd, Chern-Simons-like combination, as recently found in \cite{Bravo-Gaete:2026bdq}. This spacetime provides a concrete bottom-up arena to explore the imprints of rotation on probes in non-relativistic holography. First, we compute the holographic static quark-antiquark potential following the standard prescription that relates this boundary observable to the on shell-action of a string configuration whose endpoints are anchored at the boundary. We find that the screening length decreases both when the angular momentum is increased at fixed temperature and when the temperature is increased at fixed angular momentum. The former reflects centrifugal effects on the $q\bar{q}$ pair, whereas the latter stems from enhanced thermal fluctuations, which weaken correlations at a given separation. Second, we compute the growth rate of the Krylov complexity, using the holographic prescription that relates this observable to the momentum of a massive particle probe falling into the IR. In particular, we find that, at a given instant, the complexity grows faster as the dynamical exponent $z$ is increased.

papers.title: All known supersymmetric $\mathrm{AdS}_4 \times S^7$ uplifts from maximal supergravity
papers.abstract: The solutions of $D=4$ $\mathcal N=8$ SO(8)-gauged supergravity uplift consistently to eleven dimensions. All known supersymmetric AdS$_4$ vacua of this theory lie in an $\mathcal N=1$ truncation containing seven chiral multiplets. In this paper, we work out the uplift of this seven-chiral sector, providing a unified eleven-dimensional geometric description of all known supersymmetric AdS$_4$ solutions in this class. We then specialise to the $\mathcal N=1$ vacua with U(1)$^2$ and SO(3) symmetry, obtain their new $D=11$ uplifts and bring out their internal geometries. Both of them admit a Kaluza--Klein-type description. For the U(1)$^2$ solution, this uses the global Hopf fibration of $S^7$ over $\mathbb{CP}^3$. One U(1) acts on the fibre, while the other generates the only continuous isometry of the deformed $\mathbb{CP}^3$ base. For the SO(3) solution, the geometry takes a local non-abelian Kaluza--Klein form, with SO(3) acting on the fibres and no residual continuous symmetry on the four-dimensional base.

papers.title: FokasNets: Completing missing boundary data in Physics-Informed Neural Networks and Operators via the Global Relation
papers.abstract: We introduce FokasNets, a framework that combines Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINNs) and operators (PINOs) with the Global Relation (GR) formulation of the Fokas method (also referred to as the Unified Transform), for mixed boundary problems. The general framework considers lifted representations of the neural network models, where the Dirichlet boundary conditions are imposed by construction and the neural network learns the interior correction. The Global Relation is used as an additional solve during training that provides the missing boundary conditions to the lifted neural network, making training more efficient and accurate in the interior and on the boundary. We develop the construction of FokasNets for elliptic and evolution PDEs (Fokas-PINNs), and the corresponding PDE solution operator problems (Fokas Operator Networks - FONets), using the Global Relation formulations for these PDE classes. Furthermore, we develop the necessary theoretical framework for FokasNets, including error and stability analysis and show that FokasNets are universal approximators. We provide comprehensive numerical experiments, using examples with manufactured solutions and literature benchmarks. Compared to standard PINNs and Physics-Informed DeepONets and their lifted versions, FokasNets achieve significant improvements in solution accuracy in the interior and boundaries, both for single PDEs and particularly for solution operators, where the improvement reaches multiple orders of magnitude and fixed threshold errors are reached faster during training.

papers.title: No Cluster Left Behind I: Joint Mass Calibration for Dark Energy Survey and South Pole Telescope Clusters
papers.abstract: Multiwavelength observations of galaxy clusters are among the most promising probes of the growth of structure and dark energy. Optically identified clusters have a high number density and can thus probe the halo mass function well into the group regime, but their weak-lensing mass calibration suffers from a selection bias induced by line-of-sight projection effects. Clusters detected via their intracluster medium (ICM) -- through X-ray emission or the thermal Sunyaev-Zel'dovich effect (SZe) -- are less affected by such selection biases, but current survey sensitivity restricts ICM-selected samples to high-mass systems. Previous multiwavelength analyses tend to limit to clusters with millimeter detections and thus to the high-mass population. In this paper, we propose a flexible modeling framework in which all clusters from multiwavelength surveys can be combined and modeled, even if they are detected in only one survey. As a pilot study, we jointly model richness and lensing of clusters from the Dark Energy Survey and the SZe signal from the South Pole Telescope. This approach yields precise cluster mass calibration while self-consistently constraining optical selection biases. We have found a $\sim$20% bias in the large-scale lensing signal of clusters selected by richness, and a bias ranging from $\sim-20$% at low richness to zero at high richness for clusters selected by both richness and SZe. Compared to current approaches, this framework is highly scalable and readily extensible, paving the way for the full utilization of multiwavelength cluster data in next-generation surveys.

papers.title: Data-free continuous-time physics-informed neural networks for vortex shedding: a consistent pressure across time windows
papers.abstract: Without data, physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) in continuous time have so far failed to develop vortex shedding past a circular cylinder in a domain symmetric about the wake centerline: the training converges to the steady symmetric solution. We obtain shedding at Re=100 with a continuous-time PINN trained over successive time windows, without any reference data and without temporal discretization, the symmetry being broken by an analytical, divergence-free initial condition. The Strouhal number and the mean drag coefficient agree with an OpenFOAM solution computed on the same domain to within 0.5%. The pressure, however, is discontinuous at the junctions between windows, and the lift coefficient is a staircase. We relate this discontinuity to the differential-algebraic structure of the incompressible Navier-Stokes equations, of index 2 after spatial discretization: a consistent initial condition of each window must satisfy the constraint $\nabla\cdot\mathbf{v}=0$ for the velocity, and the hidden constraint $\nabla\cdot\partial_t\mathbf{v}=0$, with $\partial_t\mathbf{v}$ given by the momentum equation, then determines the pressure. Imposing the pressure alone makes the solution continuous but not consistent; our remedy imposes the pressure at the junctions and adds this hidden constraint to the loss. Over five shedding periods, the jumps of the lift coefficient become 20 times smaller.

papers.title: Physics-informed neural networks for quark Dyson--Schwinger equations and propagator singularities
papers.abstract: We develop a physics-informed neural-network (PINN) framework for solving the rainbow-truncated quark Dyson--Schwinger equation at real and complex momenta. The resulting dressing functions agree closely with conventional iterative solutions. We investigate the singularity structure of the quark propagator using two complementary methods. Analytic continuation of a PINN trained on the real momentum axis estimates the locations of poles and further reveals three complex-conjugate pole pairs. An independent reconstruction using PINN-parametrized spectral densities and a single pole pair yields $q=-0.146\pm0.391i~\mathrm{GeV}^2$. The agreement between the two methods substantially strengthens confidence in the properties of the leading singularities. Both spectral densities change sign, and the negative regions of the vector density and the complex poles indicate a violation of reflection positivity, consistent with quark confinement. Finally, we use the extracted poles and residues to calculate their contributions to two order parameters at finite quark chemical potential, the chiral condensate and the quark number density.

papers.title: A Realistic End-to-End Runtime Crossover Estimation for Quantum-Enhanced Training of Large-Scale Machine Learning Models
papers.abstract: Machine Learning (ML) is one promising application domain for Quantum Computing (QC) speedups, but asymptotic complexity considerations often mask the actual engineering costs of actual end-to-end workflows. For the use case of training a linearized Neural Network with a Quantum Linear Solver, a provably favorable quantum scaling has been suggested. We present realistic resource estimates for this problem, accounting for data access, computation, and readout. Our analysis examines three increasingly complex benchmarking scenarios, under distinct sparsity-scaling assumptions, thereby enabling progressively more realistic resource estimates. We identify crossover regimes relative to classical methods and find that crossover points emerge only for very large problem sizes, long computation times, and highly restrictive output requirements. This work provides a blueprint for evaluating quantum-enhanced ML algorithms under realistic hardware constraints and help identifying the bottlenecks that must be overcome to approach industrial quantum utility.

papers.title: Probe branes from equivariant volumes
papers.abstract: Classical Euclidean probe actions control non-perturbative weights and extended observables in holography. We present a geometric prescription for M2-branes in arbitrary BPS backgrounds and D3-branes in the five-form sector of type IIB. The framework accommodates compact and non-compact supersymmetric worldvolumes in both internal and spacetime directions, expressing their actions as relative equivariant pairings. Under stated extension and boundary assumptions, equivariant volumes evaluate these pairings without explicit background metrics and provide a regularization for non-compact probes. Examples in $\mathrm{AdS}_4\times SE_7$ backgrounds dual to ABJM, ADHM and flavored quiver theories reproduce and refine worldsheet-type instanton exponents and finite Wilson-loop actions. We also recover M2 giant-graviton and surface-defect actions in $\mathrm{AdS}_7\times S^4$. D3 probes in $SE_5$ compactifications dual to $\mathcal{N}=4$ super Yang--Mills and Klebanov--Witten theory provide tests involving giant gravitons, black hole probes and surface defects.

papers.title: Hamiltonian approach to isospectrality in nonrotating black holes
papers.abstract: In this work, we revisit the isospectrality of black hole perturbations from a Hamiltonian perspective. For a nonrotating, uncharged system, we present a convenient canonical description of the background degrees of freedom that facilitates comparison with the usual Lagrangian formulation. This allows us to identify phase-space counterparts of the superpotential and the algebraically special modes and show that they satisfy the expected isospectral relations, at least on shell or off shell modulo some subtle lapse redefinitions. Finally, we investigate the extent to which these results persist in theories that effectively modify general relativity. In this setting, we formally quantify the corresponding deviations from the classical relations and the associated potential violations of isospectrality to first order in the modifications.

papers.title: Machine Learning for Calabi--Yau Geometry and Heterotic Compactification
papers.abstract: Quantitative predictions from string compactification depend on geometric data that are difficult to compute analytically. This review surveys machine learning approaches to predicting topological properties of Calabi-Yau manifolds, discusses the search for new Calabi-Yau fourfolds, as well as numerical methods for approximating Ricci-flat metrics. In the context of heterotic compactifications, we explain how bundle metrics and harmonic matter forms enter calculations of canonically normalized Yukawa couplings and axion-matter interactions. We also outline applications to flux compactifications, warped and corrected backgrounds, and geometric structures beyond the Calabi-Yau setting. Finally, we review available datasets and software, highlight connections with analytic methods, and discuss geometric constraints, numerical validation, and recent progress in rigorous error control.

papers.title: Quasinormal modes of black holes in astrophysical environments: Rainbow in the dark matter
papers.abstract: Matter around black holes affects the ringdown in two ways: through the background geometry and through the response of the matter itself. We compute axial and polar gravitational quasinormal modes of a black hole embedded in a relativistic Hernquist-type dark matter halo, following the fundamental mode and the first three overtones associated with the vacuum Schwarzschild spectrum. The polar sector couples metric and matter perturbations. At small halo compactness, both sectors follow the familiar gravitational redshift law. Most of the departure from the typical redshift at larger compactness is accounted for by the exact horizon lapse factor of the background. The remaining residual departure to this lapse is sector dependent. Axial and polar frequencies are split, with their splitting growing from the fundamental through the third overtone. At large halo compactness the split grows by an order of magnitude, while overtone-to-fundamental frequency ratios depart from a common rescaling. Within the adopted dark matter profile, the halo acts on the ringdown as a prism that disperses the gravitational spectrum, leaving a parity-dependent imprint that no common rescaling of the frequencies can reproduce. Parity-isospectrality is, thus, broken.

papers.title: Chaotic singularities inside vacuum black holes
papers.abstract: According to the conjecture of Belinski, Khalatnikov and Lifshitz, general relativity gives rise to chaotic dynamics in the vicinity of generic spacelike singularities. However, no vacuum black hole has been shown to exhibit this behaviour. Here we construct stationary, asymptotically locally AdS$_5$ black holes with regular, triaxially squashed horizons and causal exteriors, whose homogeneous interiors realize the cosmological billiard of generic five-dimensional vacuum gravity. We identify a simple algebraic condition on the horizon data that is necessary for the interior billiard to be chaotic, and show that solutions with regular horizons locally access an open set of billiard trajectories.

papers.title: Neural Network Field Theory and the AdS/CFT Correspondence
papers.abstract: We develop a neural realization of massive scalar field theory on Euclidean anti--de Sitter space and its holographic boundary observables within neural network field theory (NN--FT). We construct Fourier--Bessel cosine neurons whose covariance reproduces the regulated massive AdS propagator exactly at finite network width, with the Gaussian field theory recovered in the infinite-width limit. We introduce quartic interactions through two complementary approaches. The first implements a prescribed interaction by deforming the neural parameter measure, while the second generates a local quartic interaction from the statistics of auxiliary binary neurons. Applying the BDHM prescription directly to the neural ensemble, we recover the scalar bulk-to-boundary propagator, the conformal boundary two-point function, and the leading connected four-point contact Witten diagram. We further show that distinct neural architectures can reproduce the same leading boundary correlators while defining inequivalent bulk theories. These results establish a framework for studying interacting scalar holography within NN--FT and clarify the role of neural architecture in encoding bulk dynamics and boundary observables.

papers.title: The black hole IR triangle for scalar QED
papers.abstract: We construct the black hole infrared triangle of scalar QED on a stretched Schwarzschild horizon at tree level.
